standard_prerequisites: Type families A and B over a type X, functions between their fibers, and the identity type of X with its reflexivity element.
Transport along a path in a type family, applied to functions and to elements.
Path induction with its conversion rule.
Function extensionality: the equivalence between pointwise equalities of functions and identifications of functions, together with its computation rule.
core_obligations: Prove that for functions f and g between matching fibers, the identification of the transport of f along p with g is equivalent to the family of pointwise identifications taking the transport of each element a to the transport of f of a against g at the transported point.

Identify, for the pointwise path corresponding to an identification q, the value of the evaluation map on each transported point with a three-factor concatenation built from the transport-arrow equation, the transport-concat lemma, and the unit-law lemma, closed by the component of q.
proof_roadmap: Apply path induction to reduce to the case that p is reflexivity.
In that case the claimed equivalence is exactly function extensionality between the fibers.
The moreover clause then follows from the computation rule for function extensionality, which evaluates the correspondence on each point.
difficulty_reason: A single path induction reducing to function extensionality, plus its computation rule; the care point is bookkeeping the three-factor concatenation in the second statement.
